tour.overview:
Krabi province on the Andaman coast is a land of jungle-covered limestone cliffs, mangroves, hot springs and beaches. Its most famous corner, the Railay peninsula, is cut off from the mainland by cliffs and reached only by boat, and is one of the world's great rock-climbing destinations. Inland, the lowland rainforest of Thung Teao hides pools of startling colour fed by warm springs.

This private day combines Krabi's inland wonders and its coast, with a guide, a car and a long-tail boat. You climb to the Tiger Cave Temple for the view in the cool of the morning, swim in the Emerald Pool and the hot stream waterfall, then spend the afternoon on the beaches of Railay and Phra Nang.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Krabi or Ao Nang
• Type: private tour with guide, car, driver and long-tail boat
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate to hard; the temple climb is 1,260 steep steps (optional)

WHAT YOU SEE
• Wat Tham Suea, the Tiger Cave Temple.
• The Emerald Pool and Blue Pool.
• The hot spring waterfall.
• Railay West and Phra Nang beaches.
• Phra Nang Cave.

WHY THIS WORKS
We climb the temple steps early, before the heat, reach the Emerald Pool before the day groups, and end on the beaches in the softer afternoon light.

WHO IT SUITS
Active travellers, couples and families who want jungle, swimming and beaches in one day.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer island hopping, ask us for a private boat to the Hong islands or Phi Phi.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The temple climb is steep and hot; there are monkeys on the stairs, so keep food and loose items hidden. Covered shoulders and knees are needed in the temple. Bring a swimsuit and towel.

days.name: Tiger Cave Temple, the Emerald Pool and Blue Pool, the hot spring waterfall, lunch, and Railay and Phra Nang beaches
days.description:
What to expect: Krabi's jungle pools and its most beautiful beaches, with a private guide, car, boat, fees and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 7:00 and drive to Wat Tham Suea, the Tiger Cave Temple, named after a monk who meditated in a cave where tigers once lived. A staircase of 1,260 steep steps climbs through the forest to a golden Buddha and a pagoda on the summit, 600 metres up, with a view over the karst towers, rice fields and the sea. The climb takes 30 to 60 minutes; if you prefer, you visit the caves and forest temples at the bottom instead.

You drive south-east to the Thung Teao forest, where a boardwalk through the rainforest leads to the Emerald Pool, a natural pool of warm, clear turquoise water where you can swim, and further on to the Blue Pool, too hot and mineral-rich for swimming, whose colour changes with the light. A short drive brings you to the hot spring waterfall of Khlong Thom, where warm water from the springs mixes with a cool stream over rock terraces, a natural jacuzzi in the jungle. Lunch is at a local restaurant.

In the afternoon you board a private long-tail boat at Ao Nang for the ride along the cliffs to the Railay peninsula. You walk across to Railay West beach, framed by limestone walls, and along to Phra Nang beach, one of the most beautiful in Thailand, with its cave filled with wooden offerings to the princess spirit of the sea and climbers on the cliffs above. You swim and relax before the boat takes you back at sunset, and your driver drops you at your hotel at about 18:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
07:30 – Tiger Cave Temple.
10:00 – Emerald Pool and Blue Pool.
11:45 – Hot spring waterfall.
12:45 – Lunch.
14:30 – Long-tail boat to Railay.
15:00 – Railay West and Phra Nang beaches.
17:45 – Boat back to Ao Nang.
18:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The temple climb is optional and tiring; take water.
• Monkeys on the temple stairs and at Railay can snatch bags and food.
• A rock-climbing session at Railay can be added for beginners.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, guide, entrance fees, private long-tail boat, lunch, fruit and water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks, rock climbing, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Do we have to climb the 1,260 steps?
faq.answer: No. The climb is optional; you can visit the temple's caves and forest at the bottom instead.

faq.question: Can we swim in the Emerald Pool?
faq.answer: Yes, in the Emerald Pool and at the hot spring waterfall. The Blue Pool is for looking only.

faq.question: Are the entrance fees included?
faq.answer: Yes, along with the private boat and lunch.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, a Thai lunch at a local restaurant; vegetarian and other diets are easy.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, especially the pools and beaches. Child seats and children's life jackets are provided.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The pools have boardwalks; the temple climb and boarding long-tails are demanding.

faq.question: Are the monkeys dangerous?
faq.answer: They are wild and bold: keep food and bags closed, and don't feed them. Your guide helps you avoid trouble.

faq.question: Can we try rock climbing?
faq.answer: Yes. A half-day beginners' session at Railay can be added.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Thailand but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Swimwear under light clothes, sandals or water shoes, trainers for the climb, a hat and sun cream; covering clothes for the temple.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: November to April for dry weather and calm seas. From May to October boats may not run on rough days.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
